bull.t: Rapid TPV Growth And Merchant Expansion
bull.b: Sustained TPV growth above 50% for eight consecutive quarters, together with strong retention, indicates expanding payment adoption and share of wallet. Existing merchants are adding countries, products and payment methods, creating a durable base for continued volume growth and operating leverage.

A broad licensing and authorization footprint strengthens DLocal’s ability to operate across complex emerging markets and serve global merchants through one integration. Regulatory coverage can raise entry barriers, support trust with customers, and facilitate additional products and geographic expansion.

bull.t: Strong Recent Cash Generation And Profitability
bull.b: Recent cash generation closely tracking earnings supports the quality of reported profitability and gives DLocal resources to invest in technology, licensing and market expansion. Strong conversion also improves financial flexibility for capital returns while the balance sheet remains modestly leveraged.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins shows that rapid volume growth has not translated proportionally into profitability. Continued take-rate compression and payment-cost pressure could limit earnings conversion, making future growth more dependent on efficiency gains and favorable mix.

Exposure to currency movements in major operating markets can materially affect gross profit even when transaction volumes remain strong. Regional processing-cost catch-ups and pricing pressure add to this sensitivity, creating an ongoing challenge for sustaining gross-profit and operating-profit growth.

Although recent cash generation is strong, the negative 2024 cash-flow outcome demonstrates that working-capital or timing effects can produce meaningful variability. Rising leverage from historically stronger net-cash conditions further reduces flexibility if cash conversion weakens during expansion.
